subject: Operationalizing no-train + KMS routing for CuraHealth (next steps)
messages:
From: Mike Larson <mike@curahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@curahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA + no-training / KMS segregation questions

Connor - thanks for the call earlier. We sent the redline attached (CuraHealth_DPA_redline_20270816.pdf). Two priority asks from legal & infra:

1) A firm "no-training" commitment (no model updates or data usage for model improvement) with operational proof points we can validate (logs, attestations).
2) Key management routing: customer-controlled KMS for PHI fields and a clear subprocessor routing table - we need assurance that any subprocessor who touches raw tokens won't have permanent access and that transit keys are separate from any shared platform keys.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide an operational checklist or handoff that shows KMS segregation for CuraHealth tenant traffic, and
- Deliver an evidence pack (audit logs + subprocessor inventory) before contract signature?

Mike

Attachments: CuraHealth_DPA_redline_20270816.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20270816.csv

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Larson <mike@curahealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA + no-training / KMS segregation questions

Thanks Mike - appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Looping in David (legal) and Kim (ops) to scope what we can commit to and the evidence cadence. High-level responses up-front:

- No-training: Redwood can commit to a contractual prohibition on using CuraHealth interactions to update public models. We offer two operational modes:
  a) Host-only no-train (we tag tenant traffic and exclude from training pipelines), or
  b) Dedicated tenant pool (isolated runtime + KV eviction policies).

- KMS routing: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for at-rest encryption and limited-use transit keys for inference. We need to confirm whether CuraHealth requires HSM-backed wrapping at our edge or on the host GPUs.

Kim - can you outline the minimal evidence pack (logs, attestation, subprocessor snapshot) and whether we can produce a sandboxed run to demonstrate routing?

David - please advise on appropriate contract language for the operational proof clause and any escalations if we need an SLA exception.

Connor

Subject: Re: DPA + no-training / KMS segregation questions

Connor / team / Mike - quick ops note on feasibility and deliverables:

1) Evidence pack we can produce pre-signature (sanitized where necessary):
   - Subprocessor inventory snapshot (CSV) with access scopes (we can redact internal contact emails).
   - Audit log extract showing tenant-tagged request flows and mask/eviction events (7-day sample).
   - Architecture diagram showing KMS routing and which keys are customer vs platform.

2) Implementation demo for CuraHealth pilot (timeline ~2 weeks):
   - Phase 1 (3 days): Validate BYOK integration in staging and show a tenant-request trace.
   - Phase 2 (4 days): Produce an audit export and controlled run that demonstrates no-training tagging (ephemeral KV eviction).

3) On the transit keys question: we currently use ephemeral wrapping keys at the inference edge; we can provide HSM-backed wrapping in Dedicated+Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer BYOK for at-rest and an opt-in transit locking mode (require a committed dedicated pool).

Open question for legal: do we need to tie the evidence cadence (quarterly attestation) into the DPA or capture it in a separate Ops Attachment? Mioops historically prefers an ops attachment to keep SOW clean.

Kim

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Larson <mike@curahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA + no-training / KMS segregation questions

Mike / team - thanks for raising. Draft legal approach below so commercial can align with procurement:

1) Contract language: we will add a "No-Model-Improvement" clause that prohibits Redwood from using CuraHealth customer content for model training or fine-tuning. We will define permitted telemetry (metrics, anonymized perf telemetry) and exclude token-level retention for training pipelines.

2) Operational proof clause: propose an "Evidence Attachment" that:
   - Describes the artifacts Redwood will provide (audit extract format, subprocessor snapshot, BYOK confirmation).
   - Commits to a one-time pre-signature evidence delivery and quarterly attestations thereafter.
   - Notes acceptable redaction rules for PII to protect platform security.

3) KMS routing and transit keys: we can commit to BYOK for at-rest encryption and a design-level assurance for transit key segregation. For HSM-wrapped transit keys we need to classify this as Dedicated/Private-only - we will offer a "transit locking" option as an addendum for customers requiring HSM wrapping at the edge.

I suggest we offer CuraHealth the following commercial options in the SOW:
- Standard: no-training + BYOK at rest + evidence attachment (hosted)
- Enhanced: no-training + BYOK + transit-locking on dedicated pool (additional fee)

Connor / Kim, if you can confirm the evidence artifact formats and an average time to produce the pre-signature package, I'll draft the DPA language and the Ops Attachment template.

David
